content: {"action":"upsert_decision_section","body":"Hazard thresholds must use current WBGT evidence; superseded records are historical only [CLIMATE]. The central-core record CLI-046 at v6 reporting 41.8 degrees-C-WBGT is superseded, meaning it cannot serve as the active trigger for geographic staging [CLIMATE]. Current trigger evidence must come from records with current status in the CLIMATE source; no superseded value may be treated as a live threshold [CLIMATE]. Geographic staging requires that each activated zone's WBGT reading be confirmed against a current-status record before escalation, and that any superseded record be archived as historical reference only [CLIMATE]. The distinction between probability of exceedance and coverage of the trigger network is maintained: a single superseded reading does not falsify the entire staging plan, but it cannot substitute for a current observation [CLIMATE]. Falsifier: if no current-status WBGT record exists for a zone under review, that zone's staging status is unconfirmed and must not be escalated on historical data [CLIMATE]. Rollback: reverting to a prior staging decision requires a new current-status reading that supersedes the escalation trigger [CLIMATE].","heading":"Heat triggers and geographic staging"}
